thesis: The single most valuable conversion mechanism on this site is the primary signup CTA, but it is being diluted by competing CTAs and a lack of concrete value proposition, causing visitors to hesitate or leave the funnel. The homepage and pricing page both present multiple competing CTAs (Book a demo, Start for free, Get the desktop app, Contact support) alongside vague messaging like 'AI notetaker that works (magic) in the background', which fails to communicate the concrete outcome and forces users to choose among actions, bleeding conversion value.

findings.title: Competing CTAs dilute primary action
findings.summary: The homepage presents four competing CTAs, diluting the primary signup action and creating ambiguity in the first step of the funnel.
findings.problem: Multiple competing CTAs on the homepage dilute the primary signup action, creating ambiguity in the first step of the funnel.
findings.recommended_change: h1: AI notetaker that automatically records, transcribes, and summarizes meetings; cta: Start for free (primary), secondary links in nav/footer; notes: Single dominant CTA; move demo, app, support to nav/footer; add Pricing link.
findings.evidence: ctas: Book a demo | Start for free | Get the desktop app | Contact support | h1: AI notetaker that works (magic) in the background
findings.opportunity_basis: per 1,000 visitors at an assumed 2.00% baseline conversion rate and a 2.0-8.0% relative lift

findings.title: Missing trust signals above the fold
findings.summary: The homepage shows no sign of returns policy, guarantee, so a first-time visitor has nothing to offset purchase risk.
findings.problem: The homepage shows no sign of returns policy, guarantee, so a first-time visitor has nothing to offset purchase risk.
findings.recommended_change: notes: Surface review counts, the returns window and a guarantee near the primary call to action.
findings.evidence: Measured on the live homepage: no match for returns policy, guarantee.
findings.opportunity_basis: per 1,000 visitors at an assumed 2.00% baseline conversion rate and a 1.0-5.0% relative lift

findings.title: Hero lacks concrete outcome
findings.summary: The homepage headline names the product but uses vague parenthetical language, failing to explain the concrete benefit.
findings.problem: The homepage headline names the product but uses vague parenthetical language, failing to explain the concrete benefit.
findings.recommended_change: h1: AI notetaker that automatically records, transcribes, and summarizes meetings; cta: Start for free; notes: Plain-language outcome.
findings.evidence: AI notetaker that works (magic) in the background
findings.opportunity_basis: per 1,000 visitors at an assumed 2.00% baseline conversion rate and a 0.5-2.0% relative lift

findings.title: Proof headline lacks evidence
findings.summary: The social-proof headline promises results but no customer quotes, company names, or outcome data exist to support it.
findings.problem: The social-proof headline promises results but no customer quotes, company names, or outcome data exist to support it.
findings.recommended_change: h1: AI notetaker that works (magic) in the background; cta: Start for free; notes: Add attributed testimonials and specific outcomes below headline.
findings.evidence: Real teams. Real meetings. Real results.
findings.opportunity_basis: per 1,000 visitors at an assumed 2.00% baseline conversion rate and a 0.5-2.0% relative lift

findings.title: Security claim without proof
findings.summary: The enterprise-grade security claim is repeated without any supporting evidence, undermining trust at the pricing decision point.
findings.problem: The enterprise-grade security claim is repeated without any supporting evidence, undermining trust at the pricing decision point.
findings.recommended_change: h1: Every meeting, remembered.; cta: Get Started; notes: Add security certifications, compliance status, or link to security docs.
findings.opportunity_basis: per 1,000 visitors at an assumed 2.00% baseline conversion rate and a 1.0-5.0% relative lift

findings.title: CTA clutter and unclear plan mapping
findings.summary: The pricing page presents multiple similar CTAs without clear association to tiers, confusing the next step after plan selection.
findings.problem: The pricing page presents multiple similar CTAs without clear association to tiers, confusing the next step after plan selection.
findings.recommended_change: h1: Plans & Pricing; cta: Start for free (for $0), Start trial (for $9), Contact Sales (for $24); notes: Single CTA per tier, add billing toggle, add guarantee, remove generic Get Started.
findings.evidence: prices: $0 $9 /user $24 /user | ctas: Book a demo | Start for free | Get Started | Contact Sales | Get the desktop app | Contact support
findings.analysts_agreeing: Funnel Path, Form & Interaction Friction, Navigation & Information Scent

findings.problem: Contact support is surfaced as a peer CTA on conversion pages, inviting mid-funnel users to leave the purchase path.

findings.problem: The pricing page shows paid tiers without any explicit guarantee or trial terms, increasing perceived risk at the moment of commitment.

findings.problem: Per-user prices are shown without billing period or commitment details, so visitors cannot tell if the price is monthly or annual.

findings.title: Email gate blocks enterprise evaluation
findings.summary: The enterprise page asks for a business email before showing any value or pricing, creating a high-friction gate that blocks evaluation.
findings.problem: The enterprise page asks for a business email before showing any value or pricing, creating a high-friction gate that blocks evaluation.
findings.recommended_change: h1: Voicenotes for Enterprise; cta: Explore features and pricing first, then optional email; notes: Show value and pricing before email capture.
